system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel

**Do not accept the package as drafted.** This review is based on the supplied summaries and Disclosure Letter, not the underlying SPA or DD documents. Numerical positions below are proposed buyer negotiating targets, not agreed terms or assertions of market practice.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; 20% leaves the Buyer carrying substantial undiscovered risk. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Each claim must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; no automatic application to other claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**; the combined Seller thresholds could exclude meaningful losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranty notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category deadlines, and preservation of properly notified contingent claims. | **Counter at 24 months and reject universal application**; defects may emerge over two reporting cycles, with loss crystallising later. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and deadline. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, valid issue, fully paid shares and freedom from encumbrances; no basket or de minimis. | **Seek a 100%-of-price cap and materially longer survival, aligned with applicable limitation rules**; ownership and authority are essential to the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out is identified; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend to all Claims. | Express preservation of claims for Seller fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, including attributable conduct, and non-excludable statutory rights. | **Insist on an overriding carve-out from all contractual restrictions**; fraud remedies must not be neutralised indirectly by caps, deadlines or reliance exclusions. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, preferably against specific warranties; a frozen, identifiable disclosure set. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require targeted fair disclosure**; document availability is not equivalent to explaining a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Claims barred for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable from data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-imputation language**; the Seller should not shift responsibility for its warranties onto the Buyer’s diligence process. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions. | A Buyer-benefit completion condition requiring valid consent, satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions and no unacceptable amendments, fees or termination rights. | **Require effective consent and supporting evidence before Completion, waivable only by Buyer**; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment at Completion and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees through an agreed closing process. | **Require simultaneous payoff/release mechanics and an appropriate debt adjustment, without double counting**; the Buyer must not acquire a debt-burdened or encumbered business on a debt-free basis. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses described as Seller matters but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for transaction bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, with verified eligibility, timing and payment arrangements. | **Include a Seller-funded deduction, payment or retention plus residual indemnity, without double counting**; otherwise the acquired Company could bear an unpriced transaction liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership of all relevant project materials, plus protection for associated title defects, claims and remediation costs. | **Require pre-Completion cure and broaden the specific indemnity beyond the invoice amount**; unpaid fees may prevent IP transfer and cause losses exceeding AUD 180,000. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue, said not to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and legally required notifications; continuing updates and tailored protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require an investigation/remediation covenant and specific indemnity outside general thresholds, with security if warranted**; uncertainty does not establish either a confirmed breach or absence of material exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary operating costs. | Review together for timing, scope, necessity, termination rights, accruals and compliance with interim operating covenants. | **Reserve treatment pending DD-008/DD-011 review and prohibit unapproved material commitments**; neither ordinary-course treatment nor a price deduction is established by the summaries alone. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, completion obligations and fraud. | **Insert a category-by-category limitations matrix and precedence clause**; blanket wording could silently defeat negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holding 100%. | Reconciliation with corporate records and issue/transfer history; checks for encumbrances, options and competing rights; proper transfer deliverables and title warranties. | **Independently verify title and require clean-title Completion deliverables**; the register is important evidence but does not alone establish freedom from competing interests. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for relevant pre-Completion liabilities and tailored tax warranties; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties with suitable survival and caps. | **Expressly reopen both categories: seek tax survival covering relevant assessment periods/extensions and longer, risk-based IP protection**; an 18-month, 20% general regime is inadequate for potentially latent tax and core-asset risks. |

**Immediate priorities:** secure Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff/releases, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership evidence; resolve incident exposure; and prevent the general limitations from overriding these protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
